name: Jonathan
overview: Jonathan was a male priest of the Danites, as recorded in Judges 18:30. Scripture provides limited information about him beyond this unique role. No tribe or additional notes are specified for Jonathan in the biblical text.
namesAndTitles: The name Jonathan means 'gift of YHWH,' reflecting a proper Hebrew name with significant theistic meaning. This name is noted in Judges 18:30 and highlights the divine blessing implicit in his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Jonathan is identified as the father of Gershom according to Judges 18:30. Beyond this explicit relationship, Scripture does not record further family connections for Jonathan.
scriptureSignificance: Jonathan's importance in the biblical narrative rests on his role as a Danite priest and his fatherhood of Gershom. His priestly position situates him within the religious life of Israel during the period of the Judges, contributing to the spiritual leadership of the Danite tribe. This connection underscores the ongoing provision of priestly service outside the central Levitical line, reflecting the complexities of Israel's worship history.
